subject: Delta-edge outage: temporary reroute instructions and post-incident readout
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <ops@vectorscale.com>; VectorScale SRE <sre@vectorscale.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Delta-edge outage: initial notification and temporary reroute

Hi Lucas / VectorScale SRE team,

We detected a partial failure in the delta-edge peering layer affecting traffic from APAC and EU to our hosted inference clusters starting ~2029-08-22T08:50Z. Impact: elevated errors and increased latency for routed requests originating in those regions. US regional traffic is largely unaffected.

What we did immediately:
- Activated automated cross-region reroute for affected prefixes to neighboring nodes (APAC -> us-west fallback; EU -> us-east fallback).
- Enabled degraded-capacity mode to preserve throughput (some higher-latency tails expected).
- Notified on-call infra and SRE; creating consolidated incident timeline.

Temporary ask for customers:
- If you have strict geo-routing, please check that your endpoint fallback is opt-in (instructions attached).
- If you rely on IP allowlists, we provided the fallback IP ranges in the attached PDF.

Attachments: delta-fallback-diagram.pdf, reroute-ops-checklist.xlsx

We’ll send a step-by-step reroute guide within the hour. Sorry for the disruption — we’ll keep updates to a minimum cadence unless critical.

Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai

From: Lucas Chen <ops@vectorscale.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 09:28:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-edge outage: initial notification and temporary reroute

Thanks for the heads up, Mina. A couple quick clarifications:

- Can you confirm the fallback IP ranges and whether any TLS certs are changing mid-reroute? We have strict mTLS and cert pinning for critical endpoints.
- Any expected token invalidation or session resets we should prepare for?

On Thu, 22 Aug 2029 at 09:15 Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We detected a partial failure in the delta-edge peering layer affecting traffic from APAC and EU ...

—
Lucas Chen
Head of Platform Ops, VectorScale Media
ops@vectorscale.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <ops@vectorscale.com>, VectorScale SRE <sre@vectorscale.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-edge outage: initial notification and temporary reroute

Hi Lucas — quick answers while we confirm the full post-incident notes:

- TLS / certs: No cert rotation is occurring as part of the reroute; same edge certificates continue to terminate TLS. mTLS: we are preserving client certificate validation for all fallback paths. See attached delta-fallback-diagram.pdf for IP ranges and SNI mappings.
- Tokens / sessions: We do not forcibly invalidate customer tokens. Short-lived session retry may occur when requests hit the fallback and pick a different regional backend; your existing refresh flows should be sufficient.

Operational notes:
- ETA for stable fallback routing: ~20–45 minutes depending on BGP convergence at regional peers.
- We will publish traffic-shift metrics to the incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2029-08-delta-edge

If you need a fast allowlist update, send us the CIDR(s) and we’ll prioritize.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <ops@vectorscale.com>, VectorScale SRE <sre@vectorscale.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Delta-edge: actionable reroute instructions (APAC / EU customers)

Lucas — below are explicit steps we recommend for teams that need manual confirmation or have restrictive network controls. If you’ve already seen traffic normalize, you can skip step 2.

1) Verify allowlist / firewall: add these CIDRs (see attachment) to allowlisted destinations: 34.120.88.0/22, 13.225.64.0/20 (APAC fallback set) and 18.194.0.0/16 (EU fallback set).
2) If you use SNI pinning: update SNI to fallback.s.redwood.ai for callers that need predictable routing. Example curl:

   curl -v -H "Host: fallback.s.redwood.ai" \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \n     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

3) For customers using strict regional endpoints, you can temporarily point to api-us.redwood.ai or api-eu.redwood.ai depending on preference. Note: pointing to a different region may increase median latency by ~70–180ms.
4) We are not rotating certs or invalidating tokens; refresh flows are not required but recommended if you see a small number of 401 retries.

We’ll keep this thread updated with the incident timeline and will follow up with a consolidated postmortem doc and credit proposal for verified impact.

Attachments: reroute-ops-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai

From: VectorScale SRE <sre@vectorscale.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Aug 2029 11:37:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Delta-edge: actionable reroute instructions (APAC / EU customers)

Thanks — we applied the temporary allowlist updates and validated calls to fallback.s.redwood.ai. Token refresh behavior: we observed ~0.2% increased 401s during the switch window; our refresh workers caught up within 6m.

Please include a short incident timeline in your postmortem (start 08:50Z, automated reroute 08:53Z, partial recovery 10:12Z). Also, please outline credit policy for sustained errors >0.5% over a billing day.

—
VectorScale SRE Team

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <ops@vectorscale.com>, VectorScale SRE <sre@vectorscale.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Aug 2029 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Delta-edge incident: post-incident readout, timeline, and next steps

Hi Lucas / team — thank you for the quick coordination and for confirming the allowlist changes. Summary and next steps below. Full postmortem is attached and published here: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/delta-edge-2029-08

Incident summary:
- Start: 2029-08-22T08:50Z — partial peering failure in delta-edge region due to a misconfigured route advertisement at an upstream peer.
- Automated action: 2029-08-22T08:53Z — our edge routing engine triggered cross-region fallback policies; affected prefixes were shifted to us-west/us-east backends.
- Mitigation: 2029-08-22T09:05Z — customers with strict allowlists were provided explicit CIDRs and SNI fallback.
- Recovery: 2029-08-22T10:12Z — majority of traffic returned to normal; residual error rates normalized by 10:40Z.

Impact and customer guidance:
- Regions affected: APAC, EU (partial). US unaffected for normal routing.
- Observed error uplift: peak ~1.8% errors across affected prefixes; sustained beyond 0.5% for ~56 minutes.
- Tokens: no forced invalidations; observed transient 401 spike (~0.2%) during change window.

Post-incident actions we’ve taken (completed):
- Root cause: misadvertised route from third-party peer; we have a remediation plan and confirmed the peer applied the correct routes.
- Engineering: tightened BGP validation checks and added an automated test to detect similar advertisements during rollout windows.
- Customer ops: published CIDR fallbacks and SNI fallback; added an ops checklist so partner teams can quickly opt into fallback paths.

Customer credit: Based on your ask, we will propose a credit for sustained errors >0.5% over the billing day. Karthik will follow up with an exact credit calculation and HS ticket reference within 48 hours.

Next steps (requested):
- Optional 30-minute readout — can you share a 1-hour window next week for the VectorScale platform leadership + our engineering leads to walk through the timeline and verification?
- Please confirm whether you want the temporary allowlist removed or kept for another 24–48 hours (we can automate removal if you prefer).

Thank you again for the quick responsiveness. If anything else crops up, ping me directly.

Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai
